Phase 1 merged as [#1067](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1067). **Phase 2's first trace is complete, on this repo**, and it answers the one thing Phase 1 could not verify.

## The happy path, end to end (2026-08-19 23:00–23:06 UTC)

[#1074](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1074) marked `claude-task` + `claude-model:sonnet` → tick → [#1075](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1075) → session → [#1076](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1076), six minutes end to end. Every step of §16 behaved as designed:

- **Labels ensured** by the tick before anything was marked — `claude-task` exists in the picker with its colour and description.
- **Adoption**: item titled `[claudinite-work] engine/implement-request #1074`, body `Request: #1074` / `Model: sonnet`, born `task:ready`. Both marks consumed, `claude-queued` on, one comment naming the item and the family.
- **Pickup**: precondition passed, claim + hand-off + one session, item to `task:agent`.
- **The run**: the ask was a one-line test-fixture change; the PR is exactly that, no production code, ceiling respected (opened, not merged).
- **Converge**: item parked open at `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-approval`; #1074 swapped `claude-queued` → `claude-in-review` with the PR and the model named.

**The permission API answers under the executor workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** That was the open risk — the sandbox proxy-blocks `api.github.com`, so it could not be settled at landing. A failed read would have parked #1075 at `task:needs-human-failure` with the status on it; instead the verdict passed on the read. No workflow permission needed adding.

## What Phase 2 found

The item's Context rendered as two near-identical bullets — adoption writes one, the precondition added another — in the one section the session is told to read as its binding scope. [#1077](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1077) drops the precondition's.

## Still not verified, and why

The **unauthorized-mark refusal** (the plan's second Phase 2 trace). It needs an issue whose author has no push access here; every identity available to this session is the owner's, so it cannot be staged, and the adoption→pickup window the withdrawal variant would need is seconds wide (the drain follows the tick in the same run). {"number":1078,"title":"Human-only: trace the request mode refusing an unauthorized mark, live","body":"The last unverified path of the ad-hoc request mode (#1010, landed in [#1067](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1067)). It needs a **second GitHub account with no push access on this repository**, which no session has, so it is yours.

The happy path is already traced live ([#1074](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1074) → [#1075](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1075) → [#1076](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1076), 2026-08-19) and that run confirmed the permission API answers under the executor's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. What it did **not** exercise is the branch taken for somebody who is not a collaborator at all: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{login}/permission` answering **404**, which the engine reads as "no permission" rather than as a failed read.

## Why it is worth the ten minutes

That 404 is the difference between the two things this mode must never confuse:

- read as `none` → the request is **refused** and disarmed, which is the design;
- read as a failed read → the run **parks** in the failure lane, and every stranger's marked issue becomes a triage item somebody has to clear.

Both are covered by engine tests against a fake GitHub (S45, S46, S50 in `engine-tests/scheduler/queue/request-mode.test.mjs`). Neither has been seen against the real API, and the two differ by one status code.

## Steps

- [ ] **From the second account** (no push access here), open a throwaway issue — anything, one line. *While this is off: nothing to mark.*
- [ ] **From your own account**, apply `claude-task` to it. Applying the mark to somebody else's issue is meant to authorize nothing — that is the point of the trace. *While this is off: the tick has nothing to adopt.*
- [ ] **Run the tick** — wait for the hourly one, or dispatch [Claudinite scheduler](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml) with no inputs. *While this is off: the mark just sits there.*
- [ ] **Watch, on the throwaway issue**: one comment beginning "Not implementing this:", `claude-queued` removed, **no session started**. And on the work item the tick created: closed, `task:obsolete`.
- [ ] **Watch the next tick or two**: nothing re-adopts it. The disarm is what stops the refusal repeating forever.
- [ ] **Second variant, same issue**: have the second account comment `/claude go`, re-apply `claude-task`, run the tick. It must refuse again — the phrase decides nothing; the permission behind it does.
- [ ] **Positive control**: comment `/claude go` yourself, re-apply `claude-task`, run the tick. This one must run. (Skip if you would rather not spend a session; the happy path is already traced.)

## Closing condition

Both refusals observed, with the item numbers linked here, and the throwaway issue closed. If either refusal instead **parks** the item at `task:needs-human-failure`, do not close this — the 404 is being read as a failed read, and the fix is in the `request` collector's `permissionOf` (`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`).

{"number":394,"title":"Implement per-project maintenance scheduling (owner-orchestrated rollout)","body":"Implementation tracker for the per-project scheduling conversion. Design + plan merged in #391 (Refs #390).

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design — [`docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md)
- Migration plan — [`docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md)

**End state (DESIGN §8):** every repo schedules itself via a vendored hourly scheduler Action (the repo's only cron; hashed minute :10–:50) that evaluates per-task code preconditions and dispatches agent work as `[claudinite-task]` issues labeled `ready-for-agent`; a per-repo executor CCR routine fired by that label event runs each task at its declared model. `run_daily/` → `tasks//{task.mjs,task.md}`; `.claudinite/local_packs/` → `.claudinite/local/packs/` (declaration token `local/`). Fleet-scoped work (promote, discover-packs, migrations-retire, prose-to-checks, census) becomes ordinary tasks of the canon/sheepdog repos; baselining+migrations-apply become a per-repo basics self-refresh.

**Orchestration rules:** the owner drives each phase in a session; this rollout does **not** go through the regular migration-notes mechanism; the old central routine + the two GCEC triggers stay live (and are the rollback) until Phase 4; the `schedule` key in `.claudinite-checks.json` is the per-repo cutover marker, so exactly one mechanism owns a repo at any time.

**Phases (detail in MIGRATION.md):**
- [x] **Phase 0 — canon groundwork:** build `engine/scheduler/`; add `schedule` to `CONFIG_KEYS`; `local_packs`→`local/packs` (dual-root scan) + rename the canon's own; convert canon pack tasks (baselining → per-repo self-refresh, store-release → absorbs the release cron); new/rescoped checks; doc rewrites; the `schedule`-key transition guard. No behavior change until a repo declares `schedule`.
- [x] **Phase 1 — GCEC pilot:** vendor-refresh, scheduler workflow, strip the release cron, labels, move both `dev/routines/` into the gcec pack as `tasks/`, port the create-extractor triage *decision* into the precondition (fetch/scaffold stay in the task), write the `schedule` key, create the label-wired executor routine, disable the two old GCEC triggers. Soak ~1 week.
- [x] **Phase 2 — canon cutover:** canon-side tasks (promote `daily`, discover-packs `weekly`, migrations-retire `daily+1h`, prose-to-checks `daily`), `fleet` signal over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, sheepdog `fleet-census` task; canon repo gets its own scheduler + executor.
- [ ] **Phase 3 — remaining 9 consumers** (EdFringeNow, gRatio, TLDR, HelloWorldFlutterApp, EdFringeAllocator, CrosswordChat, Sheepdog, LaughCounter, ShoutsAndWhispers), batched ~3 at a time.
- [ ] **Phase 4 — decommission:** delete the central CCR trigger + both disabled GCEC triggers; remove `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `routines/fleet/`; drop the transition guard, `run_daily`/`local_packs` aliases; retire enrollment; final boxed review vs DESIGN §8.

**Independent fix (ship anytime, not gated on a phase):** `engine/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.mjs` imports `registry.mjs` but the file is `pack-registry.mjs` — active packs' RULES.md are silently not injected at SessionStart, fleet-wide. One-line fix + regression test + vendor refresh.

{"number":590,"title":"Adoption never sets the two repo settings baselining depends on — add them to bootstrap (both are scriptable)","body":"Baselining's delivery depends on two repository settings that **nothing in adoption ever sets, checks, or mentions**. `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md` has zero references to either — the only mentions anywhere in the corpus are the error strings added by #585.

Both are the direct cause of the two-day fleet stall.

## The settings

| Setting | UI | API |
|---|---|---|
| Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests | Settings → Actions → General | `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow` → `{"can_approve_pull_request_reviews": true}` |
| Allow auto-merge | Settings → General → Pull Requests | `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` → `{"allow_auto_merge": true}` |

**Both are readable and writable by script** — plain REST, no UI-only step. The matching `GET` on each returns the current value, so a conformance check could assert them rather than only bootstrap setting them.

The constraint is the credential, not the API: both require **admin** on the repo. The Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do it, so this cannot be self-healed by baselining from inside the member. It belongs to either:

- **adoption** (`adopt-claudinite`), which already runs in a session with the owner's own credentials, or
- **the sheepdog pack**, whose `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` spans the account — it could converge both settings fleet-wide alongside `fleet-freshness`, and would catch a repo whose settings were later flipped back.

The second is the stronger option: adoption sets it once, whereas the sheepdog sweep keeps it true.

## Why it matters

Without the first, the maintenance PR is never created (#585 — silent before that fix, loud after). Without the second, an `auto-merge` member's PR opens and never lands. Neither is visible from inside the member repo, and neither produced any signal until it was investigated by hand.

## Suggested scope

1. Adoption sets both over the owner's credentials, and records what it set.
2. A check (or the sheepdog freshness sweep) asserts both remain true, reporting the exact API path when they are not.
3. `adopt-claudinite` documents them, so a hand-adopted repo does not silently miss them.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/590","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":4,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-30T21:42:38Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T05:18:54Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":996,"title":"dashboard: sign-in is the only route to a usable rate limit — wire it for the fleet deployment","body":"Being logged in to github.com in the browser buys the dashboard nothing: cookies are not sent to `api.github.com` and it refuses cookie auth cross-origin. So an unconfigured deployment runs **unauthenticated at 60 requests/hour per IP**, which one fleet sweep exceeds.

The ceilings, from [GitHub's docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api):

| credential | limit |
|---|---|
| unauthenticated | 60/hr per IP |
| user token (PAT, OAuth, GitHub App user token) | 5,000/hr, shared across every app acting for that user |
| GitHub App installation token | 5,000/hr min, up to 12,500 by fleet size |
| Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` | 1,000/hr per repository |

There is no higher tier available to a page that runs as the viewer — 5,000/hr is the ceiling, and it is 83× what the deployment gets today. **The whole fix is configuring `clientId` + `exchangeUrl`** so the sign-in button exists.

Work:
- register a GitHub App for the deployment, deploy `oauth-exchange.example.mjs`, set both keys on the pack declaration (the manual half needs its own handover issue);
- until then, say so in the page: an anonymous viewer must be told what their 60/hour means and that their github.com session is not a credential.

An installation token would raise the ceiling but needs a backend holding a shared credential — it would show every viewer everything the app can see, which is not the access model this page has.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/996","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T14:01:16Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T05:17:01Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":991,"title":"Promote conformance-work-scope to blocking once the fleet carries the step","body":"#977 landed `conformance-work-scope` (core) as **advisory**, deliberately: a requirement added to the canon with no path for consumers to comply first is the #555 failure, and its sibling `conformance-workflow` is staged the same way. This issue is the mechanism that brings the promotion back rather than leaving it to memory.

## The closing condition

Every member's CI runs the work sweep — i.e. no member's world sweep reports `conformance-work-scope`. Read it off the fleet rather than off memory:

- each member's own sweep output (the advisory finding is the signal), or
- each member's workflows containing `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`.

Delivery is by the nightly converge (owner decision, 2026-08-18 — not forced): the engine file ships with the engine tree, and the `core` bump 3 → 4 ships the check. So members cannot begin complying until their next converge, and the advisory finding is what tells each one what to add.

## The promotion itself

One line in [`packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs) — `severity: 'advisory'` → `'blocking'` — plus the catalog row in `packs/core/README.md` and a `core` version bump.

**Do not promote while any member is still missing the step.** A blocking finding reds that member's next maintenance PR, and since delivery arms auto-merge — a queue for checks — a red check there does not annoy anyone: it stops the repo updating, quietly. That is #939's failure mode from the other direction.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/991","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T08:46:55Z","updated_at":"2026-08-18T08:46:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

You are triaging GitHub issues in the repo missingbulb/Claudinite, following the "single-issue-triage" procedure below EXACTLY. This is a read-mostly triage pass with occasional write actions (label/comment/close) via GitHub MCP tools only — do NOT use gh CLI (not available), do NOT push code, do NOT open/modify any PR or branch.

The local git working tree at /home/user/Claudinite is checked out at the exact current `main` HEAD (commit 2f89ecd), clean, with no local changes — use Read/Grep/Glob on it directly to verify "is this implemented in main now" claims. This is the authoritative, current state of main.

=== single-issue-triage procedure (verbatim) ===

Triage ONE open issue and take the FIRST applicable action from this list, in order. Every action defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

1. **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (state_reason `completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it landed (file/function/behavior, checked in the actual current main tree — never inferred from a linked PR merging or the issue "looking done").
2. **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict (cite the guideline/rule it conflicts with).
3. **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
4. **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it briefly.
5. **Else** → leave it alone (no action).

Every checkbox in the issue body ticked is the author's own claim the work is done — the strongest completion signal, but still just a claim: use it as a reason to run the "implemented in main" check, never as the answer by itself. Verified → close. Not verified → comment naming what's still missing (don't close). A PARTIALLY-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage as if it carried no boxes. Where the ask has no repo-side artifact (a console setting, something only a human can do), the author's own ticks ARE the closing condition — say so and close.

"Implemented in main" means the issue's actual ask is true of main's CURRENT content — confirm it there (read the actual files/code) and cite specifically what you found. If you can't point to it concretely, comment, don't close. Create the label first (via issue_write or similar) if it doesn't already exist on the repo — but in practice these labels (needs-decision, blocked, quick-win) typically already exist; just try applying it.

Return `{ action, note }` where action is one of: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left / unchanged.

**Never re-post a verdict you already posted.** Before writing anything, read the issue's existing comments (mcp__github__issue_read method get_comments) and find the most recent comment that ends with a marker line like `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->` (a marker this same triage process posts) — or, for an issue triaged before the marker existed, judge by wording that it's a prior triage verdict. If the action you are about to take is the SAME action that comment already announced, POST NOTHING, CHANGE NOTHING (don't even re-apply a label that's already there), and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since <date of that comment>' }`. Closing is never a repeat (it changes state), so if your verdict is "close" and it isn't already closed, close it regardless of prior comments.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
(where `<action>` is one of: closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win)

=== End of procedure ===

Use these GitHub MCP tools (owner=missingbulb, repo=Claudinite):
- mcp__github__issue_read (method: get, get_comments, get_labels) to read
- mcp__github__issue_write to close an issue (state: closed, state_reason: completed) or to add/set labels
- mcp__github__add_issue_comment to post a comment
- mcp__github__get_label / list labels if needed to check a label exists (or just attempt issue_write with the label and see if it errors)

=== Your batch: triage these issue numbers in missingbulb/Claudinite ===

841 409 498

For EACH issue number above, independently run the full procedure. Do not skip any. Be careful and accurate — verify "implemented in main" claims for real against the actual current file contents in /home/user/Claudinite, don't guess.

When you're done, report back a compact table: for each issue number, the action taken and a one-line note. This report is the sole thing I need — nothing else.

{"number":1003,"title":"Manual: register this fleet owner's GitHub App and deploy its token exchange","body":"Four steps no Action can take — they need a credential and a console. Until all four are done the dashboard runs **unauthenticated at 60 requests/hour per IP**, which one fleet sweep exceeds. Context in #996.

**Scope: once per fleet *owner*, not once per fleet — and not once for everybody.** One App and one exchange endpoint serve every deployment *you* own. A GitHub App carries [up to 10 callback URLs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/about-the-user-authorization-callback-url), and with **wildcard matching** a single callback of `https://.github.io/` covers every project Pages site under that host — so a new Shepherd for a new fleet of yours adds no callback at all, just the two config keys.

Somebody else adopting this pack cannot inherit it, for mechanical reasons: a private App "can only be installed on the account that owns the app. Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it", and even a public one yields a user token that "can only access resources that both the user and app can access" — so until they install it themselves their whole fleet reads *not visible to you*, and their tokens would be minted by someone else's endpoint. They register their own, or use the token box. Spelled out in the pack README (#1007).

- [ ] **Register a GitHub App** ([new App](https://github.com/settings/apps/new)) with read-only **Contents**, **Issues** and **Actions**, and *Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation* enabled. Callback URL: the deployed dashboard's page URL — or the `https://.github.io/` root with **Enable wildcard matching** ticked, which covers every future deployment on that host. Note the **client ID**, generate a **client secret**.
  - *while undone:* no sign-in button exists; every viewer is anonymous.
- [ ] **Install the App** on the account holding the fleet's repos ([installations](https://github.com/settings/installations)). Once per *account*, not per repo — a new repo under an installed account is covered by "all repositories", or added to the selection.
  - *while undone:* sign-in succeeds but the token can read nothing, so every member row reads "not visible to you".
- [ ] **Deploy the exchange** — [`oauth-exchange.example.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-dashboard/oauth-exchange.example.mjs) as-is to a worker, with the client ID and secret as its environment. One deployment serves every dashboard you own, since it holds that App's secret and nothing else.
  - *while undone:* clicking sign-in returns to a page that cannot finish, and says the exchange was unreachable.
- [ ] **Set `clientId` and `exchangeUrl`** on the deployment's `claudinite-dashboard` entry in its `.claudinite-checks.json`. Either alone does nothing — the pair is what turns sign-in on. This is the one step a new fleet of yours repeats, with the same two values.
  - *while undone:* nothing changes; the page keeps falling back to the token box.

**Closing condition:** the deployed dashboard shows *Sign in with GitHub*, one authorization gets a viewer through a full fleet sweep, and the rate pill reads `…/5000 · user`.

### Why the exchange cannot be skipped

Verified against the [authorizing-OAuth-apps docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps):

- the web flow's token exchange lists `client_secret` as **Required**, flatly — GitHub supports PKCE (`code_challenge`, S256 only) but as *additional* protection, not as a public-client mode that drops the secret;
- the device flow genuinely needs no secret ("The `client_secret` is not needed for the device flow") but it POSTs to `github.com/login/device/code` and `github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, and those are cross-origin for a page on `github.io`. The docs state "CORS pre-flight requests (OPTIONS) are not supported at this time"; a browser cannot read a response that carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` either. *(The response headers of the token endpoint could not be probed from this sandbox — the proxy denies it — so that last half is documented, not measured here.)*

A browser extension is the case where this *does* work without a server, which is why the Chrome extension flow felt server-free: an extension with host permissions is not subject to the page's CORS rules, so it can call the token endpoint itself. A static page has no such exemption.

{"number":920,"title":"sharedMount's path regex is mount-only, so the signal is dead in the canon home","body":"`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`'s `sharedMount` collector matches vendored pack files as:

```js
/^\.claudinite\/shared\/packs\/([^/]+)\//
```

The canon home runs the same engine from its repo root, where there is no `.claudinite/shared/` and the shared packs are `packs/`. So `changedPacks` is permanently empty here, and every precondition reading it is blind in the one repo whose canon moves every day:

- `grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup` can only ever wake on its local-packs arm.
- `core/update` loses the "a pack moved" arm of its overdue gate.

The two-root form the local pack's own rule prescribes:

```js
/^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?packs\/([^/]+)\/.+/
```

A local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/…`, `.claudinite/local_packs/…`) matches neither root, which is the intent.

Split out of #912 / #913, which needed the same discrimination and does it inside the pack (`packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-dedup/worker.mjs`'s `canonPackOf`, with its own tests). Landing it engine-side would let that worker read the shared form instead — worth doing, but it is engine work with two consumers, so it gets its own change rather than riding a pack PR.

{"number":942,"title":"Dashboard sign-in: register the GitHub App and deploy the code-exchange endpoint","body":"The dashboard's sign-in path is built and tested ([#935](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/935)), but it stays dormant until two things exist that only an account owner can create. Until then every deployment falls back to the token-paste box.

## Why these can't be automated

A static page cannot reuse a visitor's github.com login: session cookies are not sent to `api.github.com`, and the API refuses cookie auth cross-origin. So "no typing" has to mean an OAuth sign-in. The `code` → token exchange needs the app's **client secret** and targets an endpoint that sends **no CORS headers**, so it cannot happen in the browser — it needs one small hosted function.

## Steps

- [ ] **Register a GitHub App** (or OAuth App) on the `missingbulb` account.
  - Callback URL: the deployed dashboard's URL, exactly — e.g. `https://missingbulb.github.io/Sheepdog/`.
  - Request **read-only** Contents, Issues, Metadata and Actions.
  - Note the **Client ID**; generate a **Client secret**.
  - *While absent:* no Sign in button renders anywhere; the token box is the only way in.

- [ ] **Deploy the exchange endpoint.** Paste [`oauth-exchange.example.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/claudinite-tasks-dashboard-20xby9/engine/scheduler/dashboard/oauth-exchange.example.mjs) into a Cloudflare Worker (or Netlify/Vercel function — same handler, different wrapper). Set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to the exact page origin.
  - *While absent:* clicking Sign in would return to a page that cannot complete the exchange, so the button stays hidden — the config gates on both halves together.
  - It sees one code and returns one token. It never proxies repo data and stores nothing.

- [ ] **Install the App** on the account/org so it can see the member repos.
  - *While absent:* sign-in succeeds but repos read as 404 — the token carries no installation.

- [ ] **Write `dashboard.config.json`** beside the deployed page with `clientId` and `exchangeUrl` (see [`dashboard.config.example.json`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/claudinite-tasks-dashboard-20xby9/engine/scheduler/dashboard/dashboard.config.example.json)). It is written by the deploying site, never committed into the vendored tree.
  - *While absent:* token fallback.

## Closing condition

Loading the deployed dashboard signed out shows **Sign in with GitHub**; clicking it returns you signed in, with your avatar in the header and a repo you can read rendering — and no token ever typed.

{"number":1299,"title":"Model the decision ballot: a parked choice, answered in place","body":"Closes #1298

A `needs-human-decision` park today leaves a person two jobs the machine could carry — work out from the timeline what the choice actually was, then translate the answer into a label edit — and the answer itself is then lost: the resumed run reads nothing about what was decided.

**The flow, as modeled** (DESIGN §4.1, and the scheduler run's new job 5):

- the park writes the choice as checkboxes in **its own park comment** (one `- [ ]` per option, each saying what the resumed run would do) — it replaces nothing, it *is* the one comment a park already owes;
- a tick is **not an event**: the answer is read at the next scheduler run, so its latency is the tick's — the same wait an ad-hoc mark has (mean 6h, never over 12);
- **exactly one box** is an answer, and the item goes back to the queue *carrying the chosen option*; more than one is not an answer — the item stays parked and is told so once;
- **closing the item is the other exit**, needing none of this, which is why the ballot mints no abandon option of its own;
- **work filed behind a park hangs off the parked item**, so both exits release it: an answered item releases its follow-up when it closes, and a hand close releases it via the scheduler run's readiness backstop one tick later.

**What modeling it found** (the simulator first, then the prose — the sim's own discipline):

- **F32, a design bug caught before any engine code**: the answers must be read *before* the instantiate job. A decision park does not hold its task's lane, so the anchor keeps filing occurrences beside it — and an answer read after job 1 puts the resumed item and that occurrence in the queue together, where the same-title mutex merely serializes them into running the task **twice** rather than deduping them. Verified by reverting the ordering and watching S78 go red.
- **A ballot is spent at the item's episode boundary** — the same artifact and the same arbitration a claim gets. That is what resumes an item exactly once per tick without anything editing the checkbox back, and it needs no second artifact because every engine-written re-queue already moves that boundary.
- **The write gate is the platform's**: only a repo write can edit a bot's comment, and the most a tick can ask for is the re-queue a label edit could already perform — so the sweep reads no actor and needs none. It is also why the ballot is a comment and never the item body, which on an ad-hoc request is the requester's own author-editable issue body.

Design only — the engine implementation is separate work.

### Folders touched

```
docs/tasks-dispatch/       §4.1 (the ballot), the scheduler run's job 5 and its
                           ordering, §9's "work that waits on a decision" edge,
                           §17.2's drain-tick list, decision §15.31, and
                           SCENARIOS' section O (S74-S78) + the F32 ledger row

docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/   the model: a ballot comment written by a decision
                           park, the tick lever, the scheduler run's answer job
                           ahead of instantiation, and episode-boundary
                           arbitration of the ballot; five scenarios and the
                           coverage-map rows
```

{"number":926,"title":"The declarative vocabulary has never reached a member's local pack — fleet census, and the one key that is missing","body":"#880 closed the coded→declared question for the **canon**. This is the same question asked of the **fleet**, and the answer is different: the canon is 49/85 declared, and until today every member repo was **0**.

## Census (2026-08-16, each member's `main`, shallow clones)

Local-pack rule modules, excluding `pack.mjs` / `lib.mjs` / task workers / tests:

| repo | local packs | coded rules | declarations |
|---|---|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | 2 | 8 | 0 |
| EdFringeNow | 3 | 7 | 0 |
| VascularColoring | 1 | 7 | 0 |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| Sheepdog | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| gRatio | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| HelloWorldFlutterApp | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| LaughCounter | 3 | 10 → **5** | **2 files, 5 rules** |
| ClaudiniteCanary | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| TLDR | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| **total** | **16** | **62 → 57** | **5** |

LaughCounter's column moved today — missingbulb/LaughCounter#203 converts five, the first declarations in any member repo.

## Two members cannot carry a declaration at all

`HelloWorldFlutterApp` and `gRatio` have no `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` in their mount, so their 10 rules are not a conversion backlog — they are a **convergence** finding. Both last moved 2026-08-12. Worth reading their stamps and the head sha's runs before anything else is proposed for them, per the standing "read the member's own artifacts first" rule.

## The one missing vocabulary key, with two named customers

Every content assertion in the vocabulary predicates on a file's **text**. Two fleet rules assert about a **path's existence alone**:

- `vascular-coloring/rendered-overlays-untracked` — no tracked image under `analysis/`
- `edfringe/no-stray-package-json` — no `package.json` outside the root and a grandfathered `plan/`

`repoWide.flagFilesMatching` matches text, so today these convert only by pairing a path-selecting `scanFiles` with an always-true content regex — a hack that reads as nothing. The honest form is a `forbidPathsMatching` assertion (pattern + exceptions + `what`/`fix`), which is the exact negative of the existing `requirePaths`. Both customers exist now; I'd build it against them rather than speculatively.

## What the rest of the fleet's rules actually are

All 62 were signal-classified (transcript / git / parse / derived-scan-set / config), and ~15 read in full — so treat the per-rule verdicts below as firm and the residue as classified but not individually argued to #880's standard.

The residue falls into the same classes #880 named, and the fleet is if anything *more* weighted to them, because a local pack exists precisely to carry what the canon shelf could not:

- **Derived scan set / derived key set** — the largest group. `shouts-and-whispers/cross-tier-constant-coverage` quantifies over constants discovered in one tier and looks for them in another *and* in the guard's own `PAIRS` map; `canary/pack-shape` reads the skill names out of `pack.mjs` and checks each named file exists.
- **Needs a real parser** — `edfringe-data/normalizer-selftest-in-verify` strips `step "…"` labels out of a shell script before looking for the command, precisely because a grep for the two tokens is satisfied by the label alone.
- **Computation** — `vascular-coloring/overlay-color-contrast` parses `(r, g, b)` literals and asserts `r - g >= 60 && r - b >= 60`. No pattern language expresses that, and it should not try.
- **Imports the definition it guards** — several read a constant or list out of the very code they check, which is the class where coded is the *stronger* rung.

Two near-misses worth naming, both one key from convertible:

- `on-device-privacy/on-device-speech` (LaughCounter) — asserts an opt-out appears within **12 lines after** a construction. `andIndentedBlockBelowMatches` does not fit: the opt-out sits at the same indentation, not inside a block. A "within the next N lines" relation would convert it.
- `macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`, `signal-teardown-routing` — both assert **ordering** (a probe sits behind a gate; `SIG_IGN` precedes `resume()`), which the vocabulary has no relation for.

## Suggested order

1. Diagnose the two stale mounts — a member that cannot compile a declaration is the blocking item, and it is not about checks at all.
2. `forbidPathsMatching`, red-first against its two customers, then convert them in their repos.
3. Judge the "within the next N lines" relation on its own merits, with `on-device-speech` as the single customer — one customer may not earn a key, and #880's `matchAnyValueOfSet` is the precedent for declining.

Nothing here proposes converting the residue. The point of the census is the opposite: to have the number, and the reason for each rule that keeps its module.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/926","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","updated_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

- `sync-claudinite.sh` — the `.claudinite/.gitkeep` tracked-copy fallback (bash; can't import JS — decide whether a generated snapshot or a documented pointer suffices).
- `routines/check-fleet-coverage.mjs` `isCovered` — the `.claudinite/.gitkeep` legacy Method-B marker check.

{"number":841,"title":"pack.json migration plan: engine reader + canon conversion, then a versioned fleet migration","body":"Executes #564 (re-evaluated 2026-08-14; PR #569 reviewed for insights and closed). Owner-settled decisions this plan encodes:

- **`pack.schema.json` is authoring tooling** (editor autocomplete + documentation). Manifest conformance — field shapes, the 20-word routing cap, skills↔tree, rule-scope agreement, the accounted-for-`.mjs` guard — is **checked by the world sweep when the file is edited**, not at load. The loader stays minimal and fail-soft: parse, resolve filenames, surface unreadable/unparseable as blocking config findings (as today).
- **`detect` is data for 14 of 17 packs** (path matching + content matching, full-noun-phrase keys per the #789/#799 discipline); sibling `detect.mjs` for chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, static-website.
- **Members' local packs convert via a `basics` migration record with `applyStage`**; the routing gap that makes `basics` the carrier for an engine-owned format is #840.

Owner approval points: **two PRs** (plus one small telemetry-gated retirement PR later). Everything else lands through the members' own auto-merged update PRs.

## PR 1 — the engine reads pack.json; the whole canon converts

One PR: the reader and the corpus it reads must land transactionally, and the home (no mount, runs repo-root code) is the first consumer either way.

- [ ] `engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json` — the authoring spec; its field order is the one canonical order (no second list).
- [ ] Registry reads `pack.json`: prefers it where `pack.mjs` coexists (a half-finished conversion must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, stamps `manifestFile` so findings name the consumer's actual file. The `pack.mjs` import path stays as the tolerance branch.
- [ ] `detect` spec compiler (tracked-path + file-content matching), with the #569-style equivalence tests: each compiled spec proven to mean exactly what the arrow it replaces meant — including the near-root `maxDepth` semantics and the jwt/web-speech/leaflet content-regex shape.
- [ ] Sibling code files named from the JSON: `detect.mjs` ×3, `env.mjs` where env is a function of config (node; flutter's static shell as data if the spec carries a line list, else a second `env.mjs`), `contributed.mjs` ×2 (barriers, canary-probe); `contributes` becomes a map of pack id → rule filenames; `worldRules`/`workRules` become filename lists (manifest placement stays the scope authority — #555; `declared-checks.json` stays structural with no manifest line — #827).
- [ ] Manifest conformance moves to the world sweep: schema shape, routing word cap, skills↔tree, scope agreement, and the every-`.mjs`-at-pack-root-accounted-for guard. Author each check first and watch it fail (a deliberately broken fixture AND a live in-scope count over the real tree — a path-pattern check that reaches zero files passes silently).
- [ ] Convert all 33 canon manifests + the home's 2 local packs; genuinely unhoused comments move to each pack's README (#569's second commit has the survey).
- [ ] Repoint every `pack.mjs` reader, enumerated from `grep -rl 'pack\.mjs'` in-branch (today: `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`, sheepdog `fleet-pack-seeds`, `adopt-claudinite` interview, `converge-wiring`, the seededByDefault audit, the pack-prose narration rule, ~20 test fixtures). Fixtures author `pack.json` and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale rather than enumerating its modules.
- [ ] Full suite via `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`; conformance sweep green; both hand-maintained tallies recomputed (not incremented) if checks were added; suite re-run against current `main` immediately before merge.

**Verified in-session**: the home *is* the corpus, so a green selftest + world sweep on the converted tree is a real end-to-end run of the reader — plus one member repo attached read-only to confirm nothing in its (unconverted) mount breaks against canon-side tasks that read packs from a fresh clone.

## Between PRs — the release gate

- [ ] Run the live canary rehearsal against the merged snapshot; watch it to a terminal state (a dispatch is not a result). Note its known blind spot: it drives the worker *this ref ships*, so it cannot see a fielded-caller break — hence the next checkbox.
- [ ] Confirm nothing under `updates/*` (the flow surface fielded workers call) changed shape in PR 1; if anything did, shim per the live-cross-version-API discipline before releasing.

## PR 2 — the release and the fleet migration record, one change

Per `engine/migrations/README.md`, a record lands in the same change as the bump it names:

- [ ] `ENGINE_VERSION` 4 → 5 (the engine that reads pack.json).
- [ ] `basics` version 2 → 3, `minEngineVersion: 5` — the updater's own enforcement guarantees no member converts its local packs before holding the engine that reads the result.
- [ ] `packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-XX-local-pack-json/migration.mjs`:
  - `applyStage: { why, instructions }` — convert this repo's local packs to `pack.json` (+ sibling `.mjs` only where a manifest genuinely holds code), move manifest comments to the pack README, delete `pack.mjs`, repair the member's own pack tests.
  - `legacyPresent` probes every declared local pack (both local-pack roots) for a surviving `pack.mjs` — the fleet census reads it, so "is the fleet done" is telemetry, not memory.
  - `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the pack.json-capable registry **by content, not version stamp** — fail-safe (unreadable mount = not capable), so the record delays instead of wedging (the sheepdog-fleet-baseline lesson).

## Same-session fleet verification — not "after the nightly"

- [ ] Force the fleet baseline/update sweep with `follow`; report per-member results unasked, attaching member repos directly rather than offering to.
- [ ] Drive one member that carries local packs through its update **now**; watch the `applyStage` session convert them and the auto-merged PR land green.
- [ ] Judge freshness by each member's stamp `ref`/engine version, never `updated` alone (held stamps), and read the **status** of every API write, not just its body.
- [ ] Report the `legacyPresent` census: which members still hold a `pack.mjs`, driven by the standing update mechanism — no phase anyone must remember to close.

## Retirement — telemetry-gated, expiry-pinned

- [ ] PR 1 ships a pinned-expiry test on the both-shapes tolerance (re-check at a named engine version), so retirement has a trigger that comes to us.
- [ ] When the census reads clean **from the members' repos, not by reasoning about canon**: one small PR deletes the `pack.mjs` read branch and the legacy fixtures. The record itself stays, as history.

{"number":409,"title":"Tracking-issue freshness: keep the plan issue in sync after every merge","body":"Implementation tracker for the tracking-issue freshness check. This issue is itself an instance of the pattern it tracks — it carries the live checklist; the committed doc carries the rationale.

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design + plan — [`docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md)

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

**Decisions (resolved with the owner):** label = `plan-tracking`; issue count not enforced; a **checkbox flip** is required (a bare comment isn't enough); label precision from the transcript for the in-session rule; the once-contingent world-scope backstop is **superseded** by the nightly task, which runs with the executor session's MCP credential and has no label blind spot.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/409","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["plan-tracking"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-23T09:56:23Z","updated_at":"2026-07-30T04:45:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

[{"id":5316661692,"body":"Two more findings from the same adoption, on the owner's instruction to keep them here rather than open separate issues. Both are about **how a human-handover step is written**, so they sit one level up from the path bug above — that one is a wrong address, these are a wrong shape.

## 1. A GitHub settings step must be a deep link, not a breadcrumb trail

The handover issue this adoption produced said things like:

> Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Every one of those is a URL the agent already knows how to construct — it has the `owner/repo` — so making the human navigate is pure friction, and a breadcrumb goes stale the moment GitHub reorganizes a settings page while a URL keeps redirecting. The rule the owner asked for: **hyperlink every requested GitHub setting change, to the deepest page that exists.**

The patterns worth naming wherever this lands:

| Step | URL |
|---|---|
| New Actions secret | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions/new` |
| Actions secrets and variables | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions` |
| Workflow permissions, Actions general | `https://github.com///settings/actions` |
| Auto-merge, merge methods, general | `https://github.com///settings` |
| Branch protection / rulesets | `https://github.com///settings/branches` |
| Environments | `https://github.com///settings/environments` |

This is general to every repo the fleet adopts, not specific to the one that hit it — which is why it is here and not in that repo's local pack.

## 2. Don't ask a human to enable something GitHub enables by default

The same issue carried a checkbox for **Settings → General → "Allow squash merging"**, on the reasoning that the merge recipe squashes always. But GitHub enables all three merge methods on a new repository, so the box could only ever be already-ticked. A handover list whose items are mostly no-ops teaches the reader to skim it, which is exactly the failure mode a handover list exists to prevent.

Worth stating as a rule where the handover shape is defined: **a handover step must name a change from the platform's default.** If the default already satisfies the requirement, the requirement is met and there is nothing to hand over.

Both corrections are applied in the consuming repo's own issue ([missingbulb/Shepherd#3](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/3)) — this is the upstream half, so the next adoption does not repeat either.

One consequence of keeping all three here: this issue's title now names only the first finding. Worth retitling to something like *"bootstrap.md Part 9 path bug, plus two rules for writing human-handover steps"* if it is going to be triaged by title.

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

{"number":1317,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.

{"number":1352,"title":"Delete the engine/scheduler shims, and repoint the worker off the updates/ ones","body":"L4, **split in two**. Supersedes #1329, which treated the two shim trees as one step. They have different retirement gates and cannot go together — and merging #1329 as written would have wedged all 13 members on their next update run.

## `engine/scheduler/` — gone

Safe now: nothing in the canon imports it (only tests reference it), and it is named by member **workflow** files, which all 13 now point at the pack mount.

With it go the vendor set's two temporary rules — the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it (every stamp carries it now). The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack goes too, and `scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the engine path as a scheduler entry.

## `updates/` — kept, one more cycle

**This is the half #1329 got wrong.** The worker resolves its flows against a *fresh canon clone at HEAD*, not its own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever **its** vendored worker names — and every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` earlier today. Deleting the tree fails every member's next update at module resolution, unrepairable, because the repair *is* the update. #1329 deletes it without repointing those calls, despite its body claiming otherwise.

This repoints the worker at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`, so the next converge fields a worker that no longer needs the shim. The tree comes out in a follow-up, gated on reading the members' vendored workers — never a date.

`install.test.mjs` now pins **both** surfaces, because both are fielded. #1329 rewrote it to pin only the new one, which would have switched off the single test guarding this.

## The 21 dangling references, resolved by kind

Deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 references dangle. They are not all the same thing:

| Count | What they are | Resolution |
|---|---|---|

{"number":1105,"title":"Engine and pack versions become date-anchored `<day>.<n>`","body":"Closes #1100.

Versions were a plain monotonic counter. It orders releases, which is all the update flows need, but it says nothing about *when* one was cut: a member stamped at `6` against a canon at `13` is behind by an unknown amount of time, and every fleet surface reporting that gap makes a reader go and date it by hand.

Both the engine and every pack now version as `.` — `60820.1`, where the day part is `(year - 2020) * 10000 + month * 100 + day` and the second part is the running number of versions cut that day. Displayed with a leading `v`, as the surfaces already do.

Two decisions worth naming:

- **The year is anchored on 2020, not taken as its last digit.** A last-digit year wraps to `0` in 2030 and sorts a decade of releases underneath every 2029 one. `2026 → 6` either way, so the example holds and the ordering survives.
- **A version is a string.** `60820.10` and `60820.1` are different versions and the same float, so nothing in the corpus may parse one as a number.

### The migration technique

Every reader accepts **both** spellings. A legacy integer parses as `.0`, which sorts below every date-anchored version — exactly where a member that has not re-stamped belongs, so no fleet surface has to special-case it. The tolerance is scheduled for removal in its own change, #1106, once the fleet has converged; the parser's own comment carries that date and issue number.

Legacy integers deliberately stay in two places for now: each pack's `minEngineVersion` floor and every migration record's `version:` range, both of which are references to engine versions that really were plain counters. #1106 retires them.

Zero stays readable and is *not* a legacy version — it is the install floor (DESIGN §3), so `isVersion(0)` is true while `isDeclaredVersion(0)` is false, and a stamp at the floor still reads as "says something" rather than as absence.

### What changed, by folder

- **`engine/`** — `version.mjs` gains the format: `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `versionsEqual`, `nextVersion`, `versionDay`, and `VERSION_SOURCE`, the regex fragment the text scrapers share so the six of them cannot disagree about what a version looks like. The helpers live beside the constant rather than in a module of their own, so the engine surface a mount must carry for any of it is one file. `ENGINE_VERSION` becomes `'60820.1'`. `pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs` validates both spellings, and `checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs` reads a record's range and ranges over it through the shared comparator.
- **`updates/`** — the three planners (`engine-update`, `pack-update`, `install`) compare through `versionAbove` instead of `>` and gate on `isVersion` instead of `typeof === 'number'`.
- **`packs/`** — all 33 manifests move to `'60820.1'`. The dashboard's `fleet.mjs` and the sheepdog's `fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs` scrape and compare through the shared helpers.
- **`.claudinite/local/packs/`** — `pack-version-bumped` and `engine-release-record`, the two canon-side checks that read a version out of a diff, do the same; the first now names `nextVersion(base)` as the remedy rather than `base + 1`.
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — the `versioned-local` shape gains a second local pack carrying the date-anchored spelling. This is the `consumer-safe-change` answer: the manifest vocabulary widened, additively, and the fixture is what proves a consumer-authored manifest still validates in **both** spellings.

`ENGINE_VERSION` moving is an engine release, so it lands with its `RELEASES.md` row citing canary rehearsal [run 32371130795](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32371130795), dispatched against this branch at `1f05d43`.

### One unrelated commit, and why it is here

The second commit fixes `a long work step leaves heartbeats on its own item`, which slept a fixed 40ms against a 5ms beat interval and asserted two beats had arrived. It is red on `origin/main` — three full-suite runs out of four at eight workers — and it was red on this branch's CI twice in a row, so nothing was going to make this PR green without it. The step now polls its own item until the second beat lands, under a 5s ceiling so a heartbeat that never fires stays a failed assertion rather than a hang. It is a separate commit and nothing else in the diff touches the scheduler.

### On delivery

This changes a contract member files carry (the stamp) and the engine flow that reads it, so "will it work on every repo?" is a live question rather than a uniform-by-construction change. Driving Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, and reporting per member, belongs to whoever merges this.

{"number":1326,"title":"Extract the task surface into claudinite-tasks, move the update flows, split the wiring converge","body":"PRs A, B and C of #1317. Landed together because none of them is green alone: the vendor set's import-closure guard forces A and B into one change, and until C stops every flow from touching `.github/workflows/`, the wiring converge still needs a stub the engine no longer owns.

Closes #1325

## A — the surface moves

`engine/scheduler/*` → `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — the queue, the executor, the task contract and its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, the delivery lane, the two workflow stubs and the three operational documents. `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` become the pack's own `test/` and `test/sim/`; `SCENARIOS.md` stays in `docs/` with its links repointed.

## B — the queue's meta-machinery follows it

`task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks.

## C — updates move, and the wiring converge splits

The versioned update flows move to `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`. A pack's `updates/` is canon-internal for the same reason its `test/` is — the flows run from the canon tree the runner just fetched and reach canon-only machinery no mount carries — so the vendor set excludes the directory by name.

`engine/converge-wiring.mjs` keeps distribution wiring (hooks, rules index and its CLAUDE.md import, `.gitattributes`, badge row, the repo's own local pack). The two workflow files become `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs`, scaffolded once at adoption by bootstrap or the adopt-pack skill.

With that, **no flow computes or writes a `.github/workflows/` path**, so the withhold staging lane is retired: nothing is staged, the emptied exports still answer for a stale worker, and the flow sweeps whatever an earlier cycle left under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`.

A migration record declares `claudinite-tasks` into every member that carries a scheduler workflow — the one artifact that says what a repo actually does rather than what its declaration hoped.

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Eight modules: `work-items`, `anchors`, `delivery`, `github`, `signals`, `task-contract`, `usage-format`, `wake`. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory and nothing else. `claudinite-dashboard` declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`; every other consumer reaches it only from a `tasks/` folder, and a pack's `tasks/` now rides the tasks pack — so a mount without the queue carries no task folders and closure holds on both sides.

`wake.mjs` is its own module rather than a line in `work-items.mjs`: the dashboard loads that one unbundled in a browser, where the scheduler run's Node built-ins do not resolve.

## Compatibility

`engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` remain as one-line re-exports for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts still name the old paths. Each tree has a `legacy-entry.mjs` that rewrites `process.argv[1]` before the re-export evaluates, so a command-line entry reached through a shim still runs as the program rather than silently defining exports and exiting. `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs` additionally keeps the old four-argument signature and its own CLI, since the split changed both. All of it is a reviewed barrier exception, and PR D deletes it.

**One migration tolerance to review**: until the seeding record has converged fleet-wide, the vendor set ships `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declares it. A member's live workflows name its modules by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be fixed by any later converge. The removal condition is stated at the code — no member's stamp lacking the pack, not a date.

## Three behaviour changes worth a look

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts the pack entry path **and** the legacy engine one, so a member's un-convergeable workflow file is not a blocking finding during the window.
- `task-declaration-shape` skips a `task.mjs` that only re-exports another module: a relocation shim declares nothing of its own. Tested by seeing it fail without the guard.
- The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse the withhold lane, which this PR retires. Its manifest now says so; **what to do with the pack is left open** rather than decided here.

## Not in this PR

PR D, the gated tail that deletes the shims once L1–L3 confirm no member names one. `implement-request` also stays a built-in under `queue/tasks/` rather than becoming an ordinary pack task — that changes its wire id, so it belongs with the decode work.

[{"id":5228468778,"number":1301,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"Stop stamping secrets by name into the executor workflow — pass the whole secrets context once","body":"Sub-issue of #1296, addressing its stamping half.

## The problem

`.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` names every secret it passes, and the wiring converge regenerates that list from `required_secrets` plus configured endpoint tokens (`converge-wiring.mjs:106-117`). That makes the file's content a function of the task set — and it is the one file a converge **cannot write**, because Actions refuses the `GITHUB_TOKEN` under `.github/workflows/` and the refusal rejects the whole ref.

So every new secret or endpoint token needs a human-merged PR in every member. #1296 is what that costs: `hitbut` had `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` set the whole time, but its live executor workflow predated the stamping, the agent could not start, and the only lane that delivers a staged workflow is the agentic apply stage the agent was needed for. Permanently wedged.

## The change

Actions has exactly one way to pass all of them: `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}`, which expands the whole `secrets` context into one variable. (`secrets: inherit` does not help — it is reusable-workflow-call only, and the callee still names each one.)

The executor step carries one static line:

```yaml
CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
```

and the workflow stops being a function of the task set. Nothing about secrets can wedge a member's workflow delivery again.

The executor then parses that bag and, per task, hands code-work **only the names that task declared**. That is a tightening, not a loosening: today `code-work-run.mjs:67` spreads the executor's whole `process.env` into the child, so all three stamped secrets reach the work step of every code-work task though only 6 of ~22 declare one — contradicting `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md:1286` ("whose env carries exactly the declared names"). Parsing a bag is what makes that line true.

`invoke.mjs` reads its endpoint token from the same bag, and its error message can finally distinguish the two causes #1296 says it conflates.

## Compatibility

Fielded members keep an old executor workflow that stamps names directly and sets no `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS`, and that file moves only by human-merged PR — so the reader accepts both: the bag when present, `process.env[NAME]` when it is not. Retirement is gated on no member still running a stamping executor workflow, never a date.

## Known cost

Every repo secret reaches the executor **job**'s env (not any task subprocess, which is filtered). And masking is registered per exact literal, so a secret containing `"`, `\` or a newline appears JSON-escaped in the bag and would not be masked if something printed it — theoretical for token-shaped values, but real. Recorded here rather than discovered later.

1	// THE OPERATOR HOLD (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §8, decision §15.24). One repository
2	// Actions variable stops the whole queue: every Claudinite workflow stamps it
3	// into its env, and every engine entry point checks it as its FIRST act — before
4	// any read, like the dormancy gate beside it — and exits cleanly having fired
5	// nothing.
6	//
7	// Why a variable rather than a commit: cancelling one run means "move on", an
8	// intent the failure continuation and the leash already serve. Stopping the
9	// SYSTEM is a different intent, and the only lever that existed for it was
10	// dormancy, which needs a commit and a converge to take effect and another to
11	// undo. A variable takes effect on the next run and clears the same way.
12	//
13	// What it freezes: STARTS, and — since the drain became batched (§15.30) — each
14	// PICK inside a running drain. A run already past this gate finishes the item it
15	// holds: killing live work would leave exactly the half-done state the leash
16	// exists to recover. Nothing NEW is ever picked.
17	//
18	// Resume needs no code: clear the variable and the next scheduler run reclaims, readies and
19	// drains on its own. The impatient path is dispatching the SCHEDULER workflow, not
20	// the bare executor — the scheduler run is what re-derives the world.
21	
22	export const SUSPEND_ALL_VAR = 'CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL';
23	
24	// Deliberately narrow: a variable somebody set to `false` or `0` to mean "off"
25	// must not read as on. Anything else — unset, empty, a word — is not a hold.
26	export const isSuspended = (env = process.env) =>
27	  ['true', '1', 'yes'].includes(String(env[SUSPEND_ALL_VAR] ?? '').trim().toLowerCase());
28	
29	// THE BETWEEN-ITEMS READ (§15.30). `vars.*` reaches a run's env at START only, so
30	// a batched drain — which may legally run for hours — cannot see a hold set after
31	// it began by re-reading its own environment. This asks the API instead, once per
32	// item boundary.
33	//
34	// A read that does not answer is NOT a verdict. It falls back to the value this
35	// run started with and SAYS which path it took: a hold silently reading as "off"
36	// spends the queue the operator was stopping, and one silently reading as "on"
37	// freezes a queue nobody held. The fallback is also what the run degrades to
38	// where the token cannot read repository variables at all — the hold then reaches
39	// this drain only when it next starts, exactly as it did before the drain
40	// batched, and every boundary says so rather than looking like a live check.
41	export async function readSuspendedNow(gh, repo, { env = process.env, log = () => {} } = {}) {
42	  const { status, json } = await gh(`/repos/${repo}/actions/variables/${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR}`);
43	  // Parsed by the same predicate as the env copy: two spellings of "is this on"
44	  // would eventually disagree, and this one decides whether work stops.
45	  if (status === 200) return isSuspended({ [SUSPEND_ALL_VAR]: json?.value });
46	  // Not set is not a fault: the variable simply does not exist, which is the
47	  // normal state of every repo nobody has ever held.
48	  if (status === 404) return false;
49	  log(`! could not read ${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR} live (${status}) — using the value this run started with.`
50	    + ' Reading a repository variable needs a token with variables read access; without it a hold'
51	    + ' reaches a running drain only when its next run starts.');
52	  return isSuspended(env);
53	}
54	
55	// The one line every entry point prints when it parks, so a run that did nothing
56	// says WHY it did nothing — a silent clean exit is indistinguishable from a run
57	// that found no work.
58	export const suspendedNotice = () =>
59	  `- ${SUSPEND_ALL_VAR} is set: the queue is held. Nothing is picked up, created, readied or reclaimed.\n`
60	  + '  Clear the variable in repo settings (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables) to resume;'
61	  + ' the next scheduled scheduler run recovers everything on its own.';
