1	# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
2	# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
3	# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
4	# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
5	name: Claudinite executor
6	
7	on:
8	  issues:
9	    types: [labeled]
10	  workflow_dispatch:
11	    inputs:
12	      continuation_depth:
13	        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
14	        required: false
15	        type: string
16	
17	permissions:
18	  contents: write
19	  issues: write
20	  pull-requests: write
21	  actions: write
22	
23	jobs:
24	  execute:
25	    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
26	    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
27	    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
28	    if: >-
29	      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
30	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
31	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
32	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
33	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
34	    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
35	    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
36	    timeout-minutes: 350
37	    steps:
38	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
39	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
40	        with:
41	          node-version: 24
42	      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
43	        env:
44	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
45	          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
46	          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
47	          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
48	          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
49	          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
50	          #
51	          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
52	          # claudinite:secrets
53	        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs
54	
55	  continue-the-chain:
56	    needs: execute
57	    if: failure() || cancelled()
58	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
59	    permissions:
60	      actions: write
61	      issues: write
62	    steps:
63	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
64	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
65	        with:
66	          node-version: 24
67	      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
68	        env:
69	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
70	          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
71	        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs

241	The script already ran the world sweep and printed its findings. On a repo with existing code,
242	**expect a backlog** — enforcement scope is whole-repo, and findings in code you never touched
243	would otherwise fail every future run. Fix causes, or record a reasoned `accept` in
244	`.claudinite-settings.json` for the deliberate keeps. Don't reach for `--changed` to hide the
245	backlog — it is a transitional aid, never the enforcement default. Commit the adoption as one
246	change referencing the adoption issue, and push it through the normal PR flow.
247	
248	## Part 9 — cloud environment setup (Claude Code on the web)
249	
250	The web base image ships no toolchains; installs belong in the environment **image** (built
251	once, snapshotted), not a per-session hook. That field belongs to the container's configuration
252	rather than the checkout, so this is a hand-over step — the owning pack declares it, the script
253	prints it in the HANDOVER block, and the fast path's last step files it. The script to paste is a
254	pack's, not core's —
255	[`packs/README.md`](packs/README.md#environment-requirements) names it and the pack that owns it.
256	Its body is identical for every project: paste it whole into the environment's **Setup script**
257	field and rebuild (`find .claudinite/shared -name environment-setup-command.sh` locates it in a
258	mount). It runs each active pack's declared installs
259	(`env.mjs install`, driven by the declaration); the SessionStart `env.mjs check` then only
260	*probes* and halt-gates on a genuinely missing prerequisite. The network policy must reach what
261	the active packs install from (npm registry, `pub.dev`, …) — the corpus itself is already in the
262	checkout.
263	
264	## Bespoke merge policy (optional)
265	
266	The portable merge recipe ships as the merge skill and needs nothing from you (squash via PR,
267	gate on CI only when the repo has it). Only if your project genuinely diverges: put the policy in
268	its own file and **name it explicitly in your `CLAUDE.md`** — the recipe reads it only then.

1	# Making changes to Claudinite without hurting consumers
2	
3	> **Status: provisional — beliefs, not law.** Every entry here says what we're *currently* doing
4	> and *why we think* it helps. When an entry blocks a better change, challenge the entry rather
5	> than contorting the change; being cited in this guide is not, by itself, a reason something
6	> must stay. We'll solidify entries once they've earned it.
7	
8	Claudinite is vendored into every consuming repo, so a change here lands in many places, on the
9	fleet's schedule, usually with no human watching. This guide collects what we currently believe
10	about making such changes safely. It is a maintainer document for sessions working *in* this
11	repo; it is not part of the vendored corpus.
12	
13	## First, know which channel the change travels
14	
15	Since the fleet moved to the tracked vendored mount (vendoring/DESIGN.md, phases 1–3 complete),
16	the channel model is small — nothing reaches a consumer instantly, and nothing arrives outside
17	its git history:
18	
19	- **The vendored corpus** (`engine/`, `packs/` — checks, prose, bundled skills) — each member
20	  holds a tracked snapshot under `.claudinite/shared/`, converged **whole-set** to the canon
21	  head by the nightly refresh and stamped with its provenance. Propagation lags one nightly,
22	  lands as a reviewable commit on the member's `claudinite/maintenance` PR (auto-merged on
23	  `auto-merge` delivery once the repo's checks pass, held for the owner on `review`), and the
24	  rollback story is the same channel: fix the canon, the next nightly re-heals. A wrong
25	  *blocking* check still fails every member's Stop hook — visible and recoverable, but
26	  fleet-wide noise, so treat check changes as production changes.
27	- **Migration notes** (`engine/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/`) — the channel for anything convergence
28	  can't express: renames of consumer-held wiring, declaration rewrites, one-off agentic steps.
29	  Stamp-day-gated and idempotent; the note's `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has
30	  moved and (for `retire: 'auto'`) retires the record itself.
31	- **Copied artifacts** (pack `stubs/`, seeded configs) — these do **not** propagate at all. Each
32	  consumer holds its own copy, which drifts silently unless a check enforces its shape. Changing
33	  the source file alone only affects repos bootstrapped *after* the change.
34	- **Bootstrap wiring** (the committed artifacts [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) seeds:
35	  `settings.json` hook registrations, the two gitignore lines, the pack declaration) —
36	  propagates through the nightly update's idempotent backfills on the same delivery PR.
37	  The discipline: a change here is written as steps that **converge from every layout in the
38	  wild**, not just from the latest.
39	
40	Out-of-repo state remains the one channel git never reaches: a web environment's pasted Setup
41	script is snapshotted at environment build. A change that moves what the pasted script calls
42	needs the script's own probe to fail fast and a member issue asking for the one human action
43	(re-paste).
44	
45	## Migrating a copied artifact (stubs and the like)
46	
47	Because copies won't move on their own, we currently migrate them through the conformance
48	checks, in one Claudinite-only change:
49	
50	1. Change the source artifact in the pack (the stub under `packs/<pack>/stubs/`).

{"number":1329,"title":"Delete the legacy shims left by the claudinite-tasks extraction","body":"PR D of #1317 — the gated tail. Written now so the stack takes one approval, **merged only at chain link L4**.

Closes #1328

> ⚠️ **Do not merge yet.** L1 must show every member's stamp carrying the pack, L2 must repoint each member's workflow `run:` lines and routine prompts, and L3 must observe a full queue cycle running from the new paths. Merging before that leaves members whose live workflows name files this PR deletes, with nothing able to repair them.

Based on `claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq` (#1326), so the diff shows only the deletion.

## What goes

- `engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` — both shim trees, each with its `legacy-entry.mjs`.
- The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack.
- The vendor set's two temporary rules: the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it. Past L3 the declaration decides, with nothing added to it.

## Two tests carry the confirmation

The point of the chain is that the retirement is *observed*, not assumed, so the tests say which:

- `engine-pack-lane-shims` gains a `RETIRED` list holding `engine/scheduler/*`. The condition for putting a path there is written at the definition: its fielded callers were read and found gone — never "the current tree does not import it", which is the one thing the scan exists because you cannot rely on.
- The fielded-flow surface in `install.test.mjs` names the flows at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`, which is the same fact from the other side: a worker one cycle behind loads them from the canon tree it just fetched.

Two canon call sites that had been going through the `updates/` shim now name the real path; one dangling link in the canary pack's README is repointed.

## Verification

Full suite 0 failures; `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops from 142 to 84 — the difference is the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/         deleted
updates/                  deleted
vendoring/                the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out
.claudinite-settings.json the engine/scheduler barrier exception comes out

1	// basics task: update — the versioned engine/pack update flows, run by a repo on
2	// itself (#768 — see the versioned-updates design there). The successor to
3	// `baselining`, and since Phase 5 deleted that, the only thing that maintains a
4	// member's mount: there is no mechanism flag left to consult, and the block that
5	// held one is gone (#1252).
6	//
7	// Two stages, like baselining's. The DETERMINISTIC flows are `code_work`
8	// (worker.mjs): they converge the mount, run the version-ranged migrations, gate on
9	// the converged tree's self-test, open the PR, and act on the terminal. The AGENT
10	// stage runs only when the pack flow's apply stage is needed — the pack's new rules
11	// meeting member-authored content the canon has never seen.
12	//
13	// Self-contained (imports nothing) so the scheduler, executor, and a human all load
14	// it standalone — the whole contract lives in this default export.
15	
16	export default {
17	  id: 'update',
18	  frequency: 'daily',                    // the head of the morning chain — everything that reads a converged mount declares `schedule_after:` this
19	  precondition_signals: ['stamp', 'sharedMount'],
20	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                 // the apply stage only — most runs are agentless
21	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',
22	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
23	
24	  code_work: 'node worker.mjs',
25	  code_work_timeout: 900,
26	  agent_execution_timeout: 1800,
27	
28	  // PURE over the collected signals. It gates only that the worker RUNS; the worker
29	  // owns every decision after that — and that division is why this asks almost nothing.
30	  //
31	  // THE ONE QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS UNAVAILABLE HERE. "Is this member behind the
32	  // canon?" needs the canon's versions, and the scheduler Action deliberately does not
33	  // read canon (DESIGN §3.3): `stamp.canonHead` is always null and no signal carries
34	  // them. Two proxies have stood in for it and both answered a different question. A
35	  // datetime in the declaration recorded the last FULL re-vendor, so a member converging
36	  // nightly read as months overdue forever (#1252). Local movement in the window —
37	  // "the mount converged and no declared pack's files changed" — reads as "nothing
38	  // happened here lately", which is equally true of a member that is current and one
39	  // that canon moved past an hour after its own converge (#1344). The second proxy left
40	  // LaughCounter and TLDR four packs behind for a day, declining their own updates,
41	  // with no way out: a forced wake mints the item and the precondition is re-evaluated
42	  // at pick, so the force converges to a no-op.
43	  //
44	  // So it no longer guesses. The asymmetry settles it: declining wrongly costs
45	  // permanent, silent staleness nothing in the member can repair, while running
46	  // wrongly costs one converge that finds nothing and exits. A daily no-op is the
47	  // cheaper mistake by a wide margin.
48	  precondition(signals) {
49	    const stamp = signals.stamp ?? {};
50	    if (!stamp.present) {
51	      return { run: false, reason: 'no vendored mount (no installed versions) — nothing to update' };
52	    }
53	    return {
54	      run: true,
55	      reason: 'the mount is due an update pass',
56	      context: [
57	        'The deterministic flows have already run: the mount is converged, the version-ranged migrations applied, and the update PR is open.',
58	        'Your job is only the apply stage — bring this repo\'s own content in line with the updated pack rules on that branch, and verify the executor routine. Do not re-run the mechanical converge.',
59	      ],
60	    };
61	  },

content.content: packs/claudinite-tasks/calendar.mjs:27:// The retired spellings, and what each reads as. `hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that

1	// The scheduling CALENDAR — the frequency vocabulary and the anchor arithmetic
2	// (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §5). Pure and stateless: given the repo's `schedule`
3	// anchor (dailyHour, weeklyDay, monthlyDay), a frequency and a `now`, it answers
4	// exactly one question — WHEN is that frequency's most recent occurrence at or
5	// before `now`.
6	//
7	// There is no occurrence IDENTITY here, and that is the point: under the
8	// work-item queue an occurrence is identified by the item's issue number, so the
9	// calendar owns the instants and nothing else. `queue/anchors.mjs` is the only
10	// consumer of the arithmetic; the vocabulary below is what the task contract and
11	// the author-time declaration check read.
12	//
13	// All times are UTC (the `schedule` values are UTC by contract). This module
14	// never reads the clock itself — `now` is always injected — so every answer is
15	// deterministic and testable.
16	
17	// The legal frequency tokens — the vocabulary the runtime contract validates
18	// against and the author-time declaration check rejects anything outside.
19	//
20	// `manual` is the one non-cadence: a manual task has no occurrence at all, so the
21	// scheduler run never instantiates it and it runs only from an item created by hand
22	// (`queue/create-work-item.mjs`). It exists for operator levers — work that
23	// answers no recurring question but wants a task's whole apparatus (declaration,
24	// contract validation, code-work, the work item) when a human pulls it.
25	export const FREQUENCIES = ['daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'manual'];
26	
27	// The retired spellings, and what each reads as. `hourly` cannot mean anything under a cron that
28	// fires twice a day (DESIGN §17.1), and the `daily±Nh` offsets staggered dependent tasks by clock
29	// hour where `after:` (§9) declares the same intent and actually enforces it.
30	//
31	// This map is PERMANENT, not a migration window. A task declaration is member-owned data that no
32	// vendoring pass rewrites, so a member can carry a retired token indefinitely and must keep
33	// working; `task-declaration-shape` is what stops a NEW declaration naming one.
34	// EMPTIED, NOT DELETED (#1234). The map IS the tolerance, so emptying it collapses
35	// `ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES` onto `FREQUENCIES`, makes a declaration still naming a retired
36	// token fail contract validation, and leaves `normalizeFrequency` as the identity every
37	// caller can keep calling — nothing is unwired, and the next retirement fills it in again.
38	// Emptied once the fleet's own declarations were read and none named a retired token:
39	// GoogleCalendarEventCreator's `create-extractor` was the last, and moved to `daily`.
40	export const LEGACY_FREQUENCIES = Object.freeze({});
41	
42	// What a declaration may CARRY, as against what a new one may be WRITTEN with.
43	export const ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES = [...FREQUENCIES, ...Object.keys(LEGACY_FREQUENCIES)];
44	
45	// THE ONE DOOR (DESIGN §17.1). Applied by `normalizeTaskDeclaration`, so every reader downstream
46	// of a loaded declaration sees a canonical token — and there is more downstream than the
47	// calendar: `periodMs` feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs`) and the
48	// precondition's signal window (`queue/signals.mjs`). Normalizing only the anchor would leave a
49	// task that now runs daily judged stale after two HOURS, which is a spurious needs-human park on
50	// exactly the members this tolerance exists for.
51	export const normalizeFrequency = (frequency) => LEGACY_FREQUENCIES[frequency] ?? frequency;
52	
53	// The documented anchor defaults (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §2) — applied
54	// when a repo omits `schedule` or any of its keys. This is the single source of
55	// these values; the checks layer's load-time range validation
56	// (engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs) only bounds them, it does not
57	// re-declare them.
58	export const DEFAULT_SCHEDULE = { dailyHour: 4, weeklyDay: 'Sun', monthlyDay: 1 };
59	
60	// Sun-indexed to match Date#getUTCDay (0 = Sunday). Also the canonical weekday

1	// WHAT A MEMBER'S SETTINGS FILE IS CALLED — the names alone, and nothing that
2	// touches a disk to find one.
3	//
4	// The names are split out from `settings-file.mjs` because one reader has no disk:
5	// the dashboard page runs this module in a browser, unbundled, and a single
6	// `node:` import anywhere in its graph fails the page's first module load
7	// (#1286). So the two halves live apart — the vocabulary here, the `existsSync`
8	// probe that picks between the names beside it — and `settings-file.mjs` re-exports
9	// everything below, which keeps it the one import every disk-side reader needs.
10	//
11	// THE RENAME (#1252). The file is `.claudinite-settings.json`. It was
12	// `.claudinite-checks.json` when checks were the only thing a member declared, and
13	// it has not been a file of checks for a long time: it carries the pack
14	// declaration, the scheduler anchor, the installed versions and the delivery
15	// override. The old name is still READ, everywhere, because a member's file is
16	// renamed by a migration record that converges on its own schedule — and until
17	// every member has run it, both names name the same file.
18	//
19	// The tolerance is the LEGACY half of a rename with a stated end: the cleanup that
20	// deletes it is gated on no member still carrying the old name, never on a date
21	// (#1252 Phase 3).
22	
23	export const SETTINGS_FILE = '.claudinite-settings.json';
24	
25	// Retired from what anything WRITES; still read while members carry it.
26	export const LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE = '.claudinite-checks.json';
27	
28	// Both names, newest first — the read order, so a member mid-rename that somehow
29	// holds both is read from the one the migration wrote. Exported for the cross-repo
30	// readers, which have no disk to probe and must try the paths in this order over
31	// the API.
32	export const SETTINGS_FILES = [SETTINGS_FILE, LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE];
33	
34	// Is this path one of the two settings-file names? For the scans that ask whether a
35	// changed file is the declaration, which must keep answering yes for a member that
36	// has not been renamed yet.
37	export const isSettingsFile = (path) => SETTINGS_FILES.includes(String(path ?? '').split('/').pop());

input.body:
quick-win — two of the three options this issue raised are already resolved on `main`. The diagnostic fix landed: `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/invoke.mjs:117` now names both causes ("Either the repository secret is not set, or `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` does not pass it — check that this repo's executor workflow names it under the `# claudinite:secrets` marker"). And the code-side loop-break (a `toJSON(secrets)` bag, tried in #1301) was explicitly reverted: `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs:51-57` records the owner's trade — GitHub's malicious-workflow detection (#1336) parks an unattended run behind a human click on that shape, so a rare human-merged PR for a new secret is accepted instead, reinstating this issue's exact deadlock as a known, deliberate cost.

That leaves only the detection half undone: nothing under `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-roster/` reads `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` for a member stuck non-shrinking. Scope, per the issue's own sizing: one existence+age check there ("fleet-roster already reads member trees; this is one existence check away and would have caught `hitbut` on day one").

# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at [REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
